title: When the Ledger Sings
premise: In the final winter of the Republic of Vessany, Mara Marchetti works as a census clerk in the occupied port city of Caldre, hiding in plain sight fifteen years after fleeing his role as a diplomatic courier. When a sharp-eyed census taker recognizes the cipher habits of the old republic's couriers, Mara's carefully buried past resurfaces: he still carries an undelivered coded ledger containing names of collaborators and innocents alike, including Alda Renne, the woman he promised to protect who is now branded an enemy of the new regime. Hunted by both the census bureau's informants and former comrades who want the ledger destroyed, Mara must choose between erasing himself forever or delivering the ledger to save Alda, knowing its publication will also condemn friends. He delivers it at terrible cost—exposing himself, losing his forged life, and surrendering to the tribunal—but the ledger's singing testimony saves Alda and dozens of others, and Mara finds that justice outside the law was never his to give alone.
about_author: Jude Eastwick is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging the papers of dissolved governments before turning to fiction. They write historical novels about ordinary people caught in the machinery of collapsing states, and live quietly near a coastline that no longer appears on current maps.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. In occupied Caldre, census taker Ilan Voss asks Mara to recite his mother's maiden name twice, noticing the hesitation of a man rehearsing a life. Mara answers correctly, but Voss lingers over the ledger page. The beat is quiet dread: fifteen years of invisibility cracking at a single question.

chapters.title: What the Cellar Keeps
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, with a flashback to the republic's fall. Mara retrieves the old courier's cipher ledger from beneath his floorboards, remembering the night he promised Alda Renne he would deliver it if the republic died. The emotional beat is grief reawakened—the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: A Name on the Enemy List
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Reading a public notice of declared enemies, Mara finds Alda's name among those slated for transport to the interior. He learns she is alive, imprisoned in the harbor customs house. Hope and terror arrive together; the promise becomes urgent, dated, mortal.

chapters.title: The Census Taker Calls Again
chapters.summary: Ilan Voss's POV. Voss reveals he knows what Mara is—or suspects—and offers a bargain: the ledger in exchange for silence. Voss is not a zealot but a tired functionary who lost a brother to the purges. The beat is dangerous intimacy between hunter and hunted.

chapters.title: Old Comrades
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Former courier Sef Barrow finds Mara, now working for the regime's archive office, demanding the ledger be burned to protect surviving collaborators—including Sef's own sister. The beat is betrayal within loyalty; Mara realizes every path costs someone.

chapters.title: The Harbor Customs House
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Using his clerk credentials, Mara infiltrates the customs house and speaks to Alda through a grate. She refuses rescue without the ledger delivered publicly—her name cleared, not smuggled out. The beat is love sharpened into principle; she will not survive by disappearing as he did.

chapters.title: Burning the Forged Life
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara destroys his false papers, his savings, and the quiet identity of 'census clerk,' accepting that delivery means exposure. Sef warns him the tribunal will read the whole ledger, condemning the innocent alongside the guilty. The beat is mournful resolve—the price counted in advance.

chapters.title: The Night of Copies
chapters.summary: Alternating Mara and Voss POVs. Mara decodes and copies the ledger for distribution while Voss, torn, delays filing his report—one day, no more. Sef's people raid the print shop; Mara escapes with the original but a young helper is taken. The beat is escalating cost and the point of no return.

chapters.title: When the Ledger Sings
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. At Alda's tribunal, Mara walks in uninvited and reads the ledger aloud, name by name, claiming authorship of every entry. The chamber erupts; the copies surface in the crowd and among the officers themselves. Climax: justice spoken outside the law, at the price of his own neck.

chapters.title: Which Silences Keep People Safe
chapters.summary: Mara's POV, months later. Sentenced but spared execution when the ledger's revelations fracture the occupation command, Mara serves his term in the same customs house. Alda, freed, visits through the grate—reversing their first meeting. Resolution: he finally stops hiding, learning some silences were never safety, only delay.
